rationale: Examination of the available primary clinical literature confirms that the published patient cohort of germline TRA2B-associated Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome comprises exactly 13 individuals from 12 unrelated families: the initial discovery study by Ramond et al. (2023) described 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families, and the subsequent single-case report by Shatokhina et al. (2023) identified 1 additional proband. No additional clinical cohorts or patient descriptions have been documented in the provided literature.

evidence.text: Ramond et al. (2023) identified 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families with monoallelic 5' variants in TRA2B who presented with neurodevelopmental delay/intellectual disability, infantile spasms, microcephaly, and brain anomalies.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5′ coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: A total of 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families who harbored predicted loss-of-function monoallelic variants, mostly de novo, were recruited.

evidence.text: Shatokhina et al. (2023) published the second investigation of germline pathogenic TRA2B variants in humans, describing a single proband harboring a de novo c.170+1G>A splice variant in the RS1 domain.

source.title: TRA2B Gene Splice Variant Linked to Seizures and Neurodevelopmental Delay: A Second Case Study
source.quote: In this study, we report a novel splice variant in the TRA2B gene identified in a patient presenting with seizures and neurodevelopmental delay. This paper represents the second investigation of pathogenic variants in the TRA2B gene in humans

evidence.text: Recent reviews focusing on TRA2B biology and regulation, such as Swarup and Qiu (2025) and Dalgliesh et al. (2025), cite the neurodevelopmental syndrome without introducing additional human patient cohorts.

source.title: Dual Role of Transformer 2 Beta as Both a Developmental Necessity and a Disease Modulator
source.quote: Dysregulation of TRA2β has been implicated in a range of diseases, including neurological, oncological, and immune-related disorders.

new_directions.question_text: Are there milder or non-syndromic presentations of TRA2B variation located outside the 5' region or RS1 domain that escape current diagnostic criteria?
new_directions.rationale: Both known cohorts exclusively documented variants in the 5' coding region that lead to overexpression of the truncated, repressive Tra2β-3 isoform via an alternative start site. Pathogenic variants in other domains might present with distinct or attenuated phenotypes.
